38.20: 38.20 And Judah sent. The promised kid is sent as to a harlot, that is, the reproach of sin, by the Adullamite, as of one rebuking, brood of vipers, etc. But the reproach of sin did not find her, whom the bitterness of confession changed. In this deed of Judah the sincerity of justice is not seen, but the fidelity of promise. For if he kept justice by keeping chastity, he would not have gone in, as he supposed, to a harlot; but what he promised, he faithfully sent through a shepherd.
38.25: 38.25 And when she was led forth, etc. ISIDORE. Afterwards by the public signs of the ring, bracelet and staff she overcame the rashly judging Jews, whom Judah already signified; who even today also say that this is not the people of Christ nor the seed of Abraham, but the evidence of our calling, justification and glorification being brought forth, they are confounded, and will confess that we rather than they have been justified. For the Church says she has the pledges, though accused by the Jews as an adulteress of the law: but she shows the staff, sign of the passion, and the bracelet, the lawful things of the law, and the ring, pledge of immortality.
38.26: 38.26 Who, knowing them, etc. JEROME. But Judah knew, etc. In the Hebrew it is: she is justified more than I; not that she was righteous, but that in comparison with him she did less evil, not by wandering shame but by seeking children.
38.27: 38.27 When the time came, etc. That the first, called Zerah, put out a hand, and the midwife tied a scarlet thread, and he drawing back his hand, the second, called Perez, put forth his hand and came first in birth, signified that Israel would stretch out its hand in the work of the law, and draw it back polluted with the blood of the prophets and of Christ himself: but the people of the Gentiles would afterwards break forth, that the first might be last, and the last first.
38.29: 38.29 Why is the partition divided for you, etc. JEROME. For partition wall Aquila and Symmachus translated division, which in Hebrew is called Perez. From this, that he divided the little membrane of the afterbirth, he took the name of division. Hence also the Pharisees, who had separated themselves from the people as just, were called Pharisees, that is divided. Zerah is interpreted rising. Because he appeared first, or because very many just were born of him, as is said in Paralipomenon.
39.1: 39.1 So Joseph was brought down into Egypt, etc. AUGUSTINE on Genesis. Scripture returns to the order from which it had departed, to narrate those things which were done above. And he was, etc. GREGORY, Morals book VI, ch. 11 ff. Many, puffed up with human wisdom, while they look upon divine judgments contrary to their desires, etc., down to and lightens its weight, which it willingly bears.
39.7: 39.7 And after many days his mistress cast, etc. GREGORY, Morals book XXX, ch. 19. He who is lifted up by worldly successes, etc., down to for since pleasure is born of prosperity, let it be struck by the consideration of the same. His mistress cast, etc. ISIDORE. This is a figure of the Synagogue, etc., down to for whence he had descended as if to be punished, thence he freed others.
39.12: 39.12 Who, leaving his garment in her hand, etc. So the allurements of the flesh tempt us and shake the fleshly garment: but the chaste man prefers to break all bonds rather than subject himself to baseness. Who leaving, etc. GREGORY. Allegorically. Because while the Synagogue, believing Christ a mere man, wished to hold him in an adulterous embrace, he put the covering of the letter before her eyes, and made himself conspicuous to the Gentiles for knowing the power of his divinity. Hence even today, while Moses is read, a veil is upon the eyes of their heart, because the adulteress kept the garment, and lost naked him whom she held wrongly.
40.1: 40.1 These things being so done, it happened that two eunuchs sinned, etc. ISIDORE on Genesis, vol. 5. Joseph found two eunuchs in prison, etc., down to is hung on the tree of transgression. The butler of the king of Egypt, and the baker, to their lord, etc. JEROME. Where we have put chief of the cupbearers, the Hebrew has masqeh, the word which we read long ago in the name of Abraham's servant, whom we can call after the manner of the common people the butler, and to this day among the barbarians it is a position of the highest dignity to have handed the cup to the king.
40.9: 40.9 I saw before me a vine, etc. JEROME. And behold a vine in my sight, and on the vine three stocks, and itself budding three stocks. The Hebrew word signifies three tendrils, three branches or shoots, which by them are called sarigim.
40.16: 40.16 Three baskets. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis. Where in the Latin codices three baskets of flour is written, etc., down to and of every kind of baker's work in the same, namely the upper, basket.
40.20: 40.20 The birthday of Pharaoh. Pharaoh and Herod celebrated the day of their birth, because they thought that from the hour of their birth they had been kings.
41.1: 41.1 After two years Pharaoh had a dream. He thought he stood, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis, vol. 3. As Abraham's servant said, etc., down to where earthly animals dwell.
41.2: 41.2 Out of which came up seven kine, etc. JEROME, Hebrew Questions. Behold, from the river came up seven kine, beautiful to see, etc., down to joined together the Greek.
41.9: 41.9 Then at length remembering, the chief of the cupbearers, etc. Because the Gentile people at last, through the exhibition of past things, brought itself into hope of future things.
41.17: 41.17 I thought I stood, etc. The seven years, which are shown by the seven full ears or the seven fat kine, signify the spiritual gifts by which the abundance of faith overflows in bounteous piety. The seven barren and lean signify the hunger of truth and justice in the last time.
41.33: 41.33 Now therefore, etc. In this time of grace we see this fulfilled: because, apostolic doctrine abounding, ministered by the sevenfold Spirit, by divine disposition bishops and teachers were appointed in each city, who in the abundance of doctrine divinely conferred on them wrote holy books, by which, when famine of the word abounds and teachers fail, we may refresh our need.
41.34: 41.34 And the fifth part of the fruits, etc. It is to be noted that the Egyptians gather a fifth part of the crops into the king's barns: because the children of darkness, given to the five senses, care not for heavenly things: but the true Israelites give tithes, because they labor to restore the heavenly country, of which a tenth part fell. ISIDORE. Joseph gathered for seven years all the abundance of crops: that is, storing in barns the grain of the faith of the saints through the seven gifts, as through seven years, so that when the seven years of want begin, that is, when the iniquity of the seven capital crimes shall meet under Antichrist, when there shall be a famine of faith and salvation, then they may have a copious harvest of justice, lest their faith fail for want of speech.
41.38: 41.38 Can we find such another man, that is full of the Spirit of God, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis. For the third time, unless I am mistaken, the Holy Spirit is suggested to us in this book. First where it was said above, chapter 1: The Spirit moved over the waters, second where God says above, chapter 6: My Spirit shall not remain in these men, etc. Third when Pharaoh says that the Spirit of God is in Joseph: yet we do not read of the Holy Spirit as yet.
41.41: 41.41 And Pharaoh said again, etc. ISIDORE. Allegorically. Joseph, who bore the type of Christ, deserved a chariot, and a herald proclaimed before him, and Pharaoh set him over all the land of Egypt: and our Lord, after he was sold by Judas, as Joseph by his brethren, and rose from the prison of hell, ascended the chariot of the heavenly kingdom, of which it is said in Psalm 67: The chariot of God is attended by ten thousand, many thousands; and he received power of preaching and judging from the Father. Hence Philippians 2: He gave him a name which is above all names, etc. He received also the ring, that is, the pontificate of faith, by which the souls of believers are sealed with the sign of salvation, and in our foreheads and hearts through the sign of the cross the figure of the eternal king is impressed. He is clothed with a robe of fine linen, that is, with holy flesh more splendid than linen, and the robe of immortality. He received also a golden chain, that is, good understanding. The herald goes before him, that is, John the Baptist, who says, Matthew 3: Prepare the way of the Lord. He will have another herald too, because he will come in the trumpet of an angel. Behold I have appointed you over all the land of Egypt, etc. Joseph, brought out of prison, is set over Egypt; and Christ rising received the name which is above all names, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, Philippians 2.
41.43: 41.43 The herald crying out, etc. JEROME in Hebrew Questions. And a herald cried before him, and set him over all the land of Egypt. For this Aquila translated: And he cried in his sight to kneeling. Symmachus, etc., down to that according to prudence he was father of all, but according to age a very tender youth and boy.
41.45: 41.45 And he called, etc. JEROME, ibid. And Pharaoh called Joseph's name, etc., down to that the true suspicion of the Hebrews about him, which we said before, may be confirmed. And he gave him a wife, etc. AUGUSTINE as above. It is usually asked whose daughter Potiphera was, otherwise Petephres, as most have it, and corruptly, as was said above, etc., down to is not dangerous to faith, nor contrary to the truth of the Scriptures.
41.50: 41.50 And two sons were born to Joseph, etc. JEROME. Observe, on account of the question which is afterwards to be put about the sons of Joseph, that before the time of the famine, when Jacob entered Egypt, Joseph had only two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
41.56: 41.56 And Joseph opened all the barns, etc. Allegorically. Joseph saves Egypt from want of grain, and Christ frees the world from the famine of the word. Christ opened his barns into the whole earth, and by the distribution of his grain subjected all things. Unless Joseph's brethren had sold him, Egypt would have failed: unless the Jews had crucified Christ, the world would have perished. Joseph is interpreted increase or enlargement: but in that Joseph only Egypt had enlargement; in ours, the whole world. He distributed wheat; ours the word of God. Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, Psalm 18.
42.1: 42.1 And Jacob hearing that food was sold in Egypt, etc. ISIDORE on Genesis, vol. 5. There is grain in Egypt: God the Father also says, Hosea 11: Out of Egypt I called my Son. Ten of the elder go down, that is the Jews, placed under the Decalogue; whom he knowing, was not known by them; the Hebrews are known by Christ, and they do not know him; they gave him money; but Joseph, that is Christ, gave wheat, and returned the silver, because Christ is not bought with money, but by grace.
42.16: 42.16 Send one of you. Otherwise by the health of Pharaoh you are spies. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis. What is it that Joseph, a wise man, etc., down to God will be, for he will not be, but will be held.
42.22: 42.22 But they knew not, etc. AUGUSTINE, ibid. What is it that when they, penitent, spoke among themselves of Joseph, etc., down to as they had sold him into foreign provinces.
42.27: 42.27 And opening, etc. Joseph's brethren give silver, because the converted Jews let go the letter that kills and receive the spirit that gives life: yet silver is found in the mouth of the sacks, because for the fruit of spiritual understanding the splendor of eloquence is not abandoned.
42.35: 42.35 Each found, etc. Joseph's brethren gave money in the purchase of grain, but received it back with the grain, because our Joseph does not seek ours, but us. For he gives his gifts freely, and in our purchase makes us richer.
42.37: 42.37 To whom Reuben answered, etc. STRABO. Reuben said: Kill my two sons, if I bring him not back to you, etc., yet he did not obtain it. But Judah, saying: I will be guilty of sin against my father forever, prevailed, because Benjamin was committed to him. It is more therefore to be guilty of sin than to be bodily slain.
42.38: 42.38 You will bring down my gray hairs, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked whether he speaks thus of going down to hell because with sorrow, or even if sorrow were absent, as one who would go down to hell by dying? For concerning hell there is a great question, and what Scripture means by it wherever it is mentioned is to be observed.
43.11: 43.11 A little resin and honey and storax, etc. JEROME, Hebrew Questions, vol. 3. Something of resin, and honey, etc., down to because in it various spices are stored.
43.23: 43.23 Your God and the God of your father has given you treasures, etc. AUGUSTINE. It seems a lie, but it must be believed to signify something. For silver, which is given and not diminished, and which is also called proved, is perhaps that of which it is said in Psalm 11: The words of the Lord are pure words, as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times, that is, proved perfectly.
43.29: 43.29 And Joseph lifting up his eyes saw Benjamin, etc. ISIDORE. Acts IX a light shone around Paul, who was little, because he had not yet the mature age of faith. Hence he is also read to be a young man, while he kept the garments of those stoning Stephen. Joseph wept; the blindness of Paul is the weeping of Christ; Christ washed his face when Paul was baptized, through whom Christ is to be seen by very many. AUGUSTINE. The affection of a good mind is always inclined to piety. Hence in Joseph we can consider the abundance of virtues. He was chaste, when he spurned the immodesty of his mistress; wise, when with diligent investigation he tested the minds of his brethren, how they felt about their uterine brother; just in applying discipline to the offenders; pious, in the conversion of the penitent.
43.32: 43.32 Which being set, etc. Food was set apart for Joseph as for a stranger, and apart for his brethren, as foreigners by nation: and for the Egyptians also apart, as natives, who thought it profane to dine with foreigners.
43.34: 43.34 And they drank and were merry, etc. AUGUSTINE. Drunkards are accustomed to use this testimony for their defense on account of Joseph, who is commended as very wise. But this word is used for satiety in the Scriptures, hence Psalm 64: You have visited the earth and have made it drunk, because it is put in praise of blessing and the gift of God is commemorated; it appears that this drunkenness signifies satiety: for to be so drunk as drunkards are drunk is not useful even to the earth itself; since by more moisture than suffices it is corrupted; like the life of a drunkard, who does not fill himself with satiety, but drowns in a flood.
44.5: 44.5 The cup which you have stolen, etc. ISIDORE. What does it mean that Joseph's cup was found in Benjamin's sack, unless that in Paul's heart the speech of heavenly doctrine already shone forth, though he was learned in the law? But because he was not subject to God, the cup was within the sack, doctrine within the law, a lamp within a bushel. Yet Ananias, sent, laid on his hand, loosed the purse, and the silver shone, and the scales falling away as bonds, the sack loosed, that is, the veil of the law laid aside, he obtained the liberty of grace, and with unveiled face preaches the Gospel of the word.
44.15: 44.15 Know you not that there is no one like me in the science of divining? AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis, vol. 3. What this means is usually asked. Is it because it was said not seriously but in jest, etc., down to the brother being recognized whom they thought lost by them.
44.16: 44.16 To whom Judah, etc. AUGUSTINE as above. Many things in Judah's narration are said otherwise than Joseph had dealt with them, etc., down to but he who knew that he knew inserted it into the narration to move him to mercy.
45.7: 45.7 God sent me, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis, vol. 3. What is it that in other copies it is read thus: For God sent me before you, to leave a remnant of you upon the earth, and to nourish a great seed of your remnants? For this does not wholly agree, etc., down to and so all Israel might be saved.
45.10: 45.10 You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, etc. JEROME. In the Hebrew it is Gosen. Hence the error grew that the land of Goshen is in Arabia. Further, as in our codices it is written with a final m, Gessem, which by no means pleases me to signify a rained-upon land. For Gessem is turned into rain, where also in many it is found Gessem.
45.16: 45.16 And Pharaoh rejoiced, etc. These words of Pharaoh, which he spoke to Joseph about Jacob and his sons, signify the joys of the Gentile people over the conversion of the Jews. For it is a great devotion of the Church of the Gentiles that the people of Israel come to the faith, to whom, if they be converted and become partakers of the faith, she promises the spiritual riches of virtues and the grace of the Holy Spirit, which he who receives will not labor in want of good.
45.22: 45.22 But to Benjamin he gave, etc. Three hundred pieces of silver are given to Benjamin, which he received from Christ who preaches the Trinity or the cross of Christ. Hence Paul says in 1 Corinthians 2: I judged not myself to know any thing among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified. He received five changes of raiment, that is the wisdom of all the senses. Paul therefore excels in abundance of merits: but the brethren also, that is other preachers, have their grace, that is two garments apiece, that they may confess Christ God and man. Hence Proverbs 31: All her domestics are clothed with double garments, that is with mystical and moral understanding. Gifts also are sent to the father, and Christ by promised gifts invites his people. Asses carry the gifts, that is the Gentiles, useless and laborious: but now useful ones carry the gifts in the type of Christ, in the Gospel the bestower of gifts. ISIDORE. Jacob was afraid, that is the unbelieving people: but after he knew the deeds of Christ his spirit revived, and he who seemed dead is made alive by the faith of Christ's resurrection. The people of the Jews is therefore called to grace by his sons, that is by Peter, Paul and John. Judah meets him, who is interpreted confession, because confession goes before those whom perfidy possessed before: and so Joseph, that is Christ, meets, who receives the people of the Jews, now old in age, at the last time, not according to merits but according to the election of grace, and lays his hand upon his eyes, and takes away the blindness; which he put off that he might believe last who before did not think he ought to believe. Hence Romans chapter eleven: That blindness in part has happened in Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles should come in, and so all Israel should be saved.
46.26: 46.26 All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, etc. AUGUSTINE. We must see what is answered to those who by this testimony confirm that souls are propagated with bodies from parents: that souls are said for men, the whole by the part in a figurative speech, no one doubts. But how do we alienate the part itself, that is the soul, by whose name the whole man is signified, from what was said, they came out of his thighs, so that we take the flesh alone as born from him although only souls are named, the modes of speech in the Scriptures must be sought.
46.27: 46.27 And the sons of Joseph, etc. JEROME, Hebrew Questions, vol. 3. All the souls of the house of Jacob, etc., down to although many hand down that Luke, as a proselyte, was ignorant of the Hebrew letters.
46.28: 46.28 And he sent Judah, etc. JEROME, ibid. He sent Judah before him to Joseph, etc., down to they suppose the village was once so called, Arsinoite.
46.32: 46.32 And they are shepherds, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis, vol. 3. It is commended in the patriarchs that they were breeders of cattle from their boyhood, etc., down to who are to have at the end the most ordered and everlasting happiness.
47.9: 47.9 The days of my pilgrimage, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis, vol. 3. What is it that Jacob says to Pharaoh, etc., down to they do not remain in the house forever.
47.11: 47.11 But Joseph gave to his father and brethren Rameses. It is to be asked whether the land of Rameses is the same as Goshen: for they had asked this, and Pharaoh had commanded it to be given. ISIDORE. Allegorically. Joseph gave his father and brethren the best land, Goshen, supplying them with food, because famine had oppressed the land: so also the Lord to his parents, that is the patriarchs and prophets, of whom he is according to the flesh, or to all the saints, of whom he says in the Gospel, Matthew 2: These are my brethren who do the will of my Father, to these he gives the best land, of which it is said in Psalm 26: I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
47.12: 47.12 Giving them food, to every one, etc. He measured wheat to his father Joseph, yet his father did not adore him, neither when he saw him nor when he received the wheat: how then do we think the dream fulfilled, unless it contains the prophecy of a greater thing.
47.16: 47.16 Bring your cattle, and I will give you, etc. It is asked, since Joseph gathered grain for men to live on, how did the cattle live, when so great a famine prevailed, and Joseph's brethren said to Pharaoh: There is no pasture for your servants' flocks, etc. If then in that famine the pastures had failed in the land of Canaan, why had they not failed in Egypt, when the same famine was everywhere? Or, as is reported by those who know the places, in many marshes of Egypt pasture might not be lacking, even when there was a famine of grain, which usually comes by the inundation of the Nile: those marshes are said to produce pasture more abundantly when the water of the Nile rises less.
47.20: 47.20 So Joseph bought, etc. Joseph is not accused of injustice or iniquity, since his fidelity is also commended from this, that he showed favor to no person, but according to the price of the buyer repaid with even balance. Mystically, however, it signifies that all who are in the spiritual Egypt and covet its wealth are slaves. For no Egyptian is free, who is carnal and sold under sin: for Pharaoh subjected them; hence perhaps it is said in Exodus 20: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Hence Romans 6: Let not sin reign in your mortal body, etc. And in the same place: You are the servants of him whom you obey, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto justice. The Egyptians were reduced to servitude by violence, the Hebrews, however, by violence into service. The Egyptians sold themselves, and it is not the fault of the dispenser where fitting recompense is made for merits. Paul also did this, when he delivered him who was unworthy of the number or fellowship of the saints to Satan, 1 Corinthians 5. Let no one then say that Paul acted too harshly who cast a man out of the Church, that being expelled he might learn not to blaspheme: for the will of man is iniquitous when, loving earthly things, he despises heavenly things, and for avarice subjects himself to the devil. But the permission of God is just when he who, spurning better things, chose worse, is let go to his own will that he may fall. So Joseph bought, etc. Allegorically the purchase of Joseph, who bought the land of Egypt with grain, signifies Christ redeeming the world by doctrine and the price of his blood. And what he says: Take seeds, and sow the fields that you may have fruits, etc., the seed is the word of God, the fields are the bodies, which, plowed by the evangelical plowshare and sown with spiritual seed, bring forth the fruit of virtues. The fifth part, which was given to the king, is the tribute of the five senses, which must be paid to Christ the King. The other four parts are allowed to the possessors for sowing and for food, because the use of the active life is granted to everyone, that he may sow works of virtue and reap the fruits of justice unto life eternal, which is bestowed on us by Christ. Hence it is said to Joseph: Our salvation is in your hand, because the salvation of the world is in the power of Christ.
47.22: 47.22 Except the land of the priests, etc. This signifies that the land of the Church, in which are the true priests, is free from worldly tribute, being fed unceasingly with the divine word, and will not suffer loss of spiritual bread.
47.29: 47.29 And when he saw the day of his death approaching, etc. AUGUSTINE, Questions on Genesis, vol. 3. He binds his son by an oath, etc., down to who appeared at baptism at about the thirtieth year.
47.31: 47.31 He swearing. AUGUSTINE as above. What the Latin codices have, He adored upon the top of his rod, some more correctly have: He adored upon the top of his own rod, or at the head of his rod, or at the tip, or upon the tip of his rod. And therefore it is rightly asked what that means which was said, etc., down to where a figure of a future thing was prefigured. JEROME. And Israel adored toward the top of his rod. In this place also some in vain pretend that Jacob adored the top of Joseph's scepter: that is, honoring his son he adored his power, whereas in the Hebrew it is read very differently: And Israel adored at the head of the bed; because after his son swore to him, secure about his request, he adored God, turned toward the head of the bed. For a holy man devoted to God, oppressed by old age, had his bed so placed that the posture of the one lying down was ready for prayer without any difficulty.
48.1: 48.1 These things being so done, taking his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim. JEROME. And he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. From this appears what we said above, that Joseph up to that point had only two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh. If after many years, at the dying of Jacob, he brought only two to the blessing, at that time when his sons could not yet beget, being little and nursing, at the entrance of the father and brethren, he could not have grandsons by them.
48.2: 48.2 Who being strengthened, etc. JEROME. And Israel being strengthened sat upon the bed. Why the Septuagint have rendered the same word one way and another I do not know, but I boldly say that the same word mittah, which here they translated bed, above, where it said Jacob adored, they named rod.
48.5: 48.5 Therefore your two sons who were born, etc. JEROME, Questions on Genesis. It is plain that seventy souls entered into Egypt, etc., down to but in the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh they will be mingled as appendages.
48.7: 48.7 For when I came out of Mesopotamia, Rachel died, and I buried her, etc. Joseph, as if not knowing, is told where and when he buried his mother, perhaps prophetically recalling that his mother was buried there where Christ was to be born.
48.12: 48.12 And when Joseph had taken them from his father's lap, etc. ISIDORE on Genesis, vol. 5. As was done in Esau and Jacob, the Lord saying: The elder shall serve the younger, so also in the sons of Joseph, etc., down to and the younger on the left made the right.
48.16: 48.16 Let my name be invoked upon them. AUGUSTINE. It is to be noted from this place that not only hearing but invocation also is said, which belong not to God but to men.
48.22: 48.22 I give you one portion, etc. JEROME on Genesis, vol. 3. I have given to you Shechem above your brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and bow. Shechem is declined according to the Greek and Latin custom, etc., down to and his mausoleum is seen there to this day. AUGUSTINE. That Jacob says he gives Shechem as a special gift to his son Joseph, and added that he had possessed it with sword and bow, it is asked how it agrees to the letter with Genesis 34. For he bought that possession for a hundred lambs, he did not take it by right of war. Or because his sons had stormed the city of Salem of the Shechemites, and by right of war it could become his, so that a just war seems to be with those who first did the injury by defiling his daughter? Why then did he not give it to his elder sons who did this? Then if now, glorying in victory, he gives it to Joseph, why did the sons who committed this displease him then? Why finally, when he blessed them, did he recall it by way of reproach? There is hidden here therefore a prophetic sacrament, because Joseph by a certain special signification signified Christ: and to him is given that land where Jacob buried the strange gods, Genesis 35, that Christ may be understood as about to possess the nations renouncing the gods of their fathers and believing in Christ.
49.1: 49.1 ALBINUS. In the blessings of Jacob the history is to be held and the allegory to be searched out: history of the division of the promised land, allegory of Christ and the Church, to be revealed in the last times; but first the foundations of the history are to be laid.
49.3: 49.3 Reuben my firstborn, etc. JEROME, Questions on Genesis. Reuben my firstborn, you my strength, and the beginning of my sons, etc., down to you have lost the order of the firstborn.
49.5: 49.5 Simeon and Levi, etc. JEROME as above. Septuagint: Simeon and Levi, brethren, have accomplished the iniquity of their invention, etc., down to into their counsel let not my soul come.
49.8: 49.8 Judah, your brethren shall praise you, etc. JEROME as above. Because Judah is interpreted confession or praise, etc., down to by the same sense, in other words, the Church is shown, of which it is said Matthew 5: A city set on a mountain cannot be hid.
49.9: 49.9 Judah is a lion's whelp: to the prey, my son, you are gone up: resting you have couched as a lion, etc. ISIDORE. Or the lion's whelp rested in sleep, because not of necessity, but of power. Hence: I have power to lay down my life, and no man takes it from me, but I lay it down of myself, John 10. What he adds, and as a lion's whelp, whence he died, thence he was born. The naturalists say that a lion's whelp, when born, sleeps three days and three nights. Then, startled by the roar of the father, the place of the den rouses the sleeper: Christ also, lying in the den of the sepulchre three nights, fulfilled the sleep of death. Well then did Christ rest as a lion, who overcame not only the bitterness of death but its dominion too, and as a lion's whelp, because on the third day he rose. Hence it is added: Who shall rouse him up? etc. None, understand, but he who says, John 2: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
49.10: 49.10 The scepter shall not be taken away from Judah, etc. For so long kings of the seed of Judah were among the Jews until Christ was born of the Virgin. For the first foreign king in the nation of the Jews was Herod, when Christ was already born. Whoever therefore denies that Christ has come, let him show a king of the tribe of Judah in the nation of the Jews.
49.11: 49.11 Tying his colt to the vineyard, etc. The Gentiles whom he has subjected to himself. Hence Ezekiel 18: As I live, says the Lord, I will clothe myself with these men as with a garment. For Christ washed us in the blood of the grape when as a cluster he hung on the wood of the cross, and from his side water went forth for washing and blood for redemption.
49.12: 49.12 His eyes more beautiful, etc. ISIDORE. Because their doctrine exceeds the austerity of the old law, and the evangelical precepts are clearer than the commandments of the law. With milk, that is the doctrine of the law, which fed the carnal or little people with milk: but whiter, the teachers of the Church, who eat and distribute the strong and robust food of the word. Hence Hebrews 5: Solid food is for the perfect, who are well called whiter than milk, because white, pure and free from every stain.
49.13: 49.13 Zebulun shall dwell on the seashore, etc. To show believers a refuge and to those in peril the harbor of faith. Established against all the bounds of the age, it awaits the shipwreck of the Jews and the storms of the heretics: who are carried about with every wind of doctrine, hence also some apostles were taken: there the Lord often taught. It reaches as far as Sidon, that is, it comes even to the Gentiles. Hence Isaiah 9: The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, etc. Sidon is hunting: and from those places hunters were taken, of whom it is said Jeremiah 16: I will send many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain.
49.14: 49.14 Issachar. JEROME, Hebrew Questions. He desired a good thing, resting between the lots, etc., down to and therefore all the tribes serve him, bearing gifts as to a master. Lying down between the borders, etc. To lie down is to rest, the end of the world being awaited, and to seek nothing of worldly things but to desire the last. A strong ass saw rest, and the best land: when simple Gentile-hood raised itself to strength of work, because it tends to the fatherland of life.
49.16: 49.16 Dan shall judge his people, etc. ISIDORE on Genesis, vol. 5. Others think that by these words Antichrist is foretold to be of the tribe of Dan, etc., down to and after the benefits of feigned sweetness he exercises the horns of power. Dan shall judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel. Let Dan be a snake in the way, a serpent in the path, biting the horse's heels, that his rider may fall backward. I will wait for your salvation, O Lord. JEROME as above. Samson, judge of Israel, was of the tribe of Dan, etc., down to and he shall be the expectation of the Gentiles.
49.19: 49.19 Gad. JEROME. A little robber shall rob before him, etc., down to and the enemies being conquered he fought bravely. Gad girded shall fight before him. ISIDORE. Christ will fight before and behind against Antichrist: before, by the hidden coming of humility; behind, by the manifested glory of majesty. Hence Moses, Deuteronomy 33: Blessed be he that enlarges Gad, he rested as a lion, and seized the arm and the top of the head, and saw his principality. For Christ rested in the sepulchre, humbled the top of the head and the pride of the lofty, and to him is given principality, and honor, and kingdom.
49.21: 49.21 Naphtali. JEROME. Allegorically. A loosened shoot, giving beauty to the nation, etc., down to because there especially he taught, as is also written in the Gospel. Naphtali a hart let loose, etc. ISIDORE. For the apostles and preachers, leaping swiftly like harts, pass beyond the hindrances of the age, and meditating on high things give words of beauty, that is preach the doctrine of the Savior.
49.22: 49.22 Joseph a growing son, etc. JEROME as above. A growing son by the fountain, etc., down to commanding also ten tribes of Israel.
49.27: 49.27 Benjamin a ravenous wolf, etc. JEROME, ibid. In the morning he shall eat the prey, and in the evening divide the spoil. Although it is a most manifest prophecy of Paul, that in his youth he persecuted the Church, in old age he was a preacher of the Gospel, etc., down to concerning the priests who, serving the altar, live by the altar, 1 Corinthians 9. Benjamin a ravenous wolf, etc. ISIDORE. Some of the teachers referred this to Jerusalem, etc., down to then he shall divide the spoil, understanding that the letter is to be divided by the spirit, because the letter kills, but the spirit gives life, 2 Corinthians 3.
49.28: 49.28 All these in the tribes, etc. It is asked why Jacob made all whom he begot of free women and of handmaids sons and heirs with equal honor? Because as Christ bestows heavenly rewards with equal honor and glory on all who are reconciled to his body through faith. For there is no distinction there whether he be Jew or Greek, Barbarian or Scythian, bond or free: because Christ is all and in all, who took the form of a servant, and served for the free and for the bond, that he might bestow an equal gift on all. Whoever deserves the faith of the Lord is obscured by no stains of carnal birth. Hence Joel 2: I will pour out of my spirit upon all flesh.
49.32: 49.32 And added, etc. STRABO. It must be asked of what people it is said? For about the fathers there is no question. It is known that he was added to Abraham and Isaac, but a people is a multitude. Those, being so few, could not be called a people. It must be understood therefore that this is said also of the angels, to whose society, passing from the world, the saints are added. Hence Hebrews 12: You are come to Mount Sion, and to Jerusalem the heavenly, and to the company of many angels, etc.
50.1: 50.1 Which Joseph seeing, fell, forty days passed. STRABO. Which number befits penance and humility. Hence in the law and in the Gospel it was observed by the prophets and by the Lord himself. AUGUSTINE. The forty days of burial which Scripture mentions perhaps signify penance, by which sins are buried. For not in vain were forty days of fasting appointed, in which Moses, and Elijah, and the Lord himself fasted, and the Church calls the chief observance of fasts Quadragesima. Hence in Jonah also it is written of the Ninevites: Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be destroyed, Jonah 3, that through so many days, suited to the humiliation of penitents, they may be understood to have wept their sins in fasting and to have obtained mercy. Nor does this number befit only the mourning of penitents. For forty days after the resurrection the Lord was with his disciples, going in and out, eating and drinking, which days were days of joy. Nor are the Seventy Interpreters to be believed to have erred who said: Three days, and Nineveh shall be destroyed: for endowed with greater authority than the office of interpreters, by the prophetic spirit by which they are affirmed to have agreed with one mouth in their interpretations, which was a great miracle, they put three days, though they knew that forty days were read in the Hebrew; that in the glorification of Christ sins might be understood to be dissolved and abolished, who was delivered for our sins and rose again for our justification. The glorification of the Lord, however, is known in the resurrection and ascension. Hence here, though he gave one and the same spirit: first after he rose, second after he ascended; and because he rose after three days, and ascended after forty days: one of these, which was done later, the Hebrews signify by the number of forty days; the other, concerning the three days, which belongs to the same thing, the Septuagint mention, not by the servitude of interpretation but by the authority of prophecy. Let us not therefore say that one of these is false, and for some interpreters contend against others; since those who interpret from the Hebrew prove that what they interpret is written, and the authority of the Septuagint, commended by so great a divinely wrought miracle, is confirmed in the Churches by so great antiquity. Seventy days. STRABO. The heathen wept for their dead nine days. Hence the ninth day was called novendial, when they were buried. The worshipers of God celebrated funeral rites seven days. Hence Ecclesiasticus 22: The mourning for the dead is seven days: but for a fool all the days of his life. For the number seven signifies rest. Hence the seventh day is called the sabbath, that is rest. They celebrate the seventh day of the dead, wishing them to rest with the Lord from the labors of the present life. Hence therefore it is said: Egypt mourned him seventy days, which is seven multiplied tenfold. For seven times ten are seventy. It can also be said that, as the third day of the dead is observed by the faithful, that the soul, which is of a threefold nature, may rest; so the seventh day is celebrated that the soul may be reconciled to the body, which sinned when the flesh enticed. In the number seven also there are three and four; three belongs to the soul, which is irascible, and concupiscible, and rational; four to the body, which consists of four elements.
50.4: 50.4 And the time of mourning being ended, etc. AUGUSTINE. What Joseph charged the great men of Egypt to say to Pharaoh in his name: My father made me swear, saying: In the sepulchre which I have made for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me; it is asked how this is true, since these words of his father, when he gave charge of burial, are not read. But the words are to be referred to the sense, as above other things similarly repeated. For words must serve the will to be expressed and brought to knowledge. That Jacob dug a sepulchre for himself is nowhere read above, but certainly, unless he had dug it, it would not be said at all.
50.10: 50.10 And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, etc. This place is beyond the Jordan, and is seventy miles from Hebron. They passed beyond therefore the place where they ought to bury him, and afterwards, the Jordan crossed, returned to the place of the double cave. Hence it may be asked why they did this. If someone says because they feared wars, as the children of Israel led about through the desert forty years until, having crossed the Jordan, they came to the promised land. But this was done for a cause of greater significance. In the place which is called the threshing floor of Atad, the multitude of the children of Israel afterwards, murmuring against the Lord, was consumed by divine fire. With so great mourning therefore was lamented not so much the death of Jacob as the future ruin of the people.
50.22: 50.22 And he lived a hundred and ten years. AUGUSTINE on Genesis, vol. 3. Since Scripture says Joseph saw in his life these sons of sons or grandsons of sons, how does it join them to the sixty-five souls with whom Jacob is said to have entered Egypt, etc., down to which was propagated while he lived, through whom it came about that he entered.
50.24: 50.24 Carry up my bones, etc. STRABO. Joseph, like his father, desired the land of promise with all his mind and detested the sojourn in Egypt. He instructs us also morally that as long as we are in this world we always desire the land of promise, that is of the living, and wish to rest there: which is well done if we imitate by our morals the number of Joseph's years. For he died having completed a hundred and ten years of life: let us also strive through the observance of the Decalogue to come to eternal beatitude, which the hundred signifies.
50.25: 50.25 Embalmed with spices. STRABO. Happy is the soul which, embalmed with the spices of virtues, living in the coffin of the body, by daily progress is reserved for unending life. If it has been kept in faith, hope and charity, by the grace of Christ it will deserve to come to the sight of divine contemplation, the adoption of which is perfect joy; hence Psalm 15: You shall fill me with joy with your countenance.
